card.name: Auxiliary verbs before an expected predicate
card.fires_on: Small helper words or adverbs (to, be, were, got, is, particularly, pleasantly, most) sitting right before the main verb or adjective in running web prose. Mostly narrative history or nature text.

modes.label: Helper verbs
modes.description: Auxiliaries like be, were, is, to right after a subject and before the main predicate.
modes.example: with a little more time, he might<< be>> able to develop new weapons

modes.label: Adverbs before adjectives
modes.description: Degree or manner adverbs that lead into an adjective.
modes.example: You might be<< pleasantly>> surprised at what you see.

card.plain: It fires on little connecting words that sit just before the main verb or descriptive word in a sentence.
